proposed_comments.title: Keep asynchronous in-memory WAV buffers valid

confidence.rationale: Microsoft PlaySound documentation explicitly requires SND_MEMORY plus SND_ASYNC buffers to remain valid until playback completes, while the current byte[] P/Invoke pin lasts only for the call.

proposed_comments.body:
### Keep asynchronous in-memory WAV buffers valid

**Severity:** `high`

`PlaySound` is called with `SND_MEMORY | SND_ASYNC`, but the current `byte[]` marshalling pin is only guaranteed for the duration of the P/Invoke. The native audio playback can therefore retain a pointer after the managed array is movable again, causing corrupted playback or an invalid memory read. Keep each lazily loaded WAV buffer pinned for the application lifetime, pass its stable `IntPtr` to `PlaySound`, and handle a `false` return as a playback failure.

proposed_comments.title: Deploy the sound files in installed builds

confidence.rationale: The MSI authoring enumerates configured directories non-recursively and has no Sounds directory/component, while the project emits both files under the Sounds subdirectory.

proposed_comments.body:
### Deploy the sound files in installed builds

**Severity:** `high`

`CopyToOutputDirectory` places the assets in the build output's `Sounds` subdirectory, but the MSI authoring neither declares that directory nor installs either WAV file. Installed PowerToys builds will therefore always take the missing-sound path even though local project builds work. Add a `Sounds` installer directory/component containing `open.wav` and `close.wav`, include it in `RunComponentGroup`, and remove the directory on uninstall.

proposed_comments.title: Exercise the non-default settings and allow winmm

confidence.rationale: Both per-event switches now default true; the current opening=true assignments are no-ops, and the fork spell-check directly required winmm as a one-word allow entry.

proposed_comments.body:
### Exercise the non-default settings and allow `winmm`

**Severity:** `medium`

After the per-event defaults changed to `true`, the opening-sound assignments in the CLI and view-model tests stopped exercising that setter. Set the opening option to `false`, make the view-model test drive all three properties away from their defaults and expect three IPC callbacks, and add `winmm` as its own entry in the spell-check allow list so the new P/Invoke does not fail the spelling gate.

proposed_comments.title: Align the PR description with the implementation

confidence.rationale: The live body says the bundled Freesound assets are purpose-recorded and all three toggles default false, while NOTICE and code identify existing CC BY recordings and true per-event defaults.

proposed_comments.body:
### Align the PR description with the implementation

**Severity:** `medium`

The summary describes purpose-recorded custom sounds and says all three settings default to `false`, while `NOTICE.md` identifies existing Freesound recordings and the code defaults both per-event switches to `true`. Update the description to call them bundled third-party CC BY 3.0 assets and document that the parent defaults off while opening and closing default on. This keeps the reviewed provenance, compatibility behavior, and validation contract consistent.
